title: Vulnerability lifecycle: audit schema, RBAC v2 integration, and triage automation proposal
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc proposes a unified audit event schema and RBAC v2 integration for vulnerability lifecycle events, plus a triage automation flow and SIEM export mapping. Goal: make triage decisions auditable, connect scanner outputs to assignment/workflows, and ensure evidence is available for audits and postmortems.

High-level objectives:
- Define minimal, consistent audit fields for every vuln lifecycle change (ingest -> triage -> patch -> verify -> close).
- Ensure RBAC v2 role model supports least-privilege triage and remediation handoffs.
- Provide SIEM mapping and sourcetypes for vendor scanners, enrichment services, and remediation actions.
- Automate routine triage and assignment where safe; provide human-in-the-loop for policy exceptions.
- Track patch SLAs and enable automatic escalations and rollback traces.

RBAC v2 role recommendations (surface-level):
- vuln_reader: read-only access to vulnerability records, evidence metadata, and audit history. Intended for engineering teams and auditors.
- vuln_triage: can change triage state, set severity/owner, add comments, request patching. Cannot mark resolved.
- vuln_remediator: can create patch jobs, update remediation steps, and mark verification steps complete.
- vuln_owner: full lifecycle control for assigned product/component; can close issues and request exceptions.
- vuln_auditor: read audit trail and evidence, export events to compliance buckets.
- system_ingest: machine principal for scanners and enrichers.

RBAC enforcement notes:
- All role assignments should be scoped by resource tags (component, org unit, cloud-project) to avoid global privileges.
- Use time-limited role grants for 3rd-party contractors and emergency escalations.
- Record role-grant and role-revoke events into the same audit stream with the same schema.

Proposed audit event schema (flat fields for SIEM-friendly ingestion):
- event_type: one of [scanner_ingest, enrichment, triage_update, assignment, patch_created, patch_applied, verify_result, close, sla_violation, sla_escalation, role_grant, evidence_upload]
- event_id: stable UUID for the event
- vuln_id: canonical vulnerability identifier (internal id + external ids if present)
- scanner_id: identifier of scanner or parser (e.g., oss-scan-v2, snyk, docker-scan)
- severity_before: severity prior to event (if applicable)
body_continued:
- severity_after: severity after the event (if applicable)
- action: human-readable short action verb (triage_set, assign, annotate, patch_request, patch_apply, rollback)
- actor_id: principal id (user/email or machine principal)
- actor_role: resolved RBAC role at time of action
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- evidence_refs: list of evidence identifiers (S3 path or artifact id)
- evidence_hashes: comma-separated list of content hashes stored in evidence index
- patch_reference: link to patch job or PR (URL)
- patch_version: artifact/version applied
- rollback_reference: link to rollback action (if any)
- sla_deadline: ISO-8601 deadline computed at assignment time
- assigned_team: team tag for owner
- comment: free-text note (max length heuristics enforced at ingest)

Notes on schema design:
- Keep schema flat (no nested objects) to simplify Splunk/ELK ingestion and queries. Fields that would be lists are stored as comma-separated strings.
- Use consistent enumerations for event_type and actions so alerting rules can be simple.
- Include both actor_id and actor_role to detect privilege changes and suspicious activity.

SIEM export mapping (recommended sourcetypes / indices):
- Index: sec_vuln_lifecycle
- Sourcetype: vuln:lifecycle:event
- Field mapping examples:
  - vuln_id -> vuln_id
  - event_type -> event_type
  - actor_id -> user
  - actor_role -> user_role
  - timestamp -> _time
  - evidence_refs -> evidence_paths
  - evidence_hashes -> evidence_hashes
  - sla_deadline -> sla_deadline
  - patch_reference -> patch_url

- Additional parsers: build a lightweight parser that normalizes scanner IDs into canonical scanner_id and enriches with severity_cvss when available. Enrichment jobs add severity_cvss, cve_ids, and first_seen timestamps as separate fields.

Triage automation flow (stepwise):
1) Scanner(s) produce normalized ingest events with scanner_id and raw findings.
2) Ingest service normalizes to internal vuln_id; runs dedupe and fingerprinting.
3) Enrichment: OSV/SCA feeds, CVE metadata, historical exploit telemetry attached.
4) Rule engine evaluates: if severity >= critical OR exploit_present -> auto-assign to vuln_owner + create patch job and set SLA based on severity map.
5) For medium/low: if fingerprint matches allowed exception list OR package is non-production -> mark as mitigated (annotated) and close automatically when policy allows.
6) All automated actions require event entry with actor_role=system_ingest and reason tag. Humans must be able to override with triage comments; override events recorded.

Severity -> SLA mapping (proposed):
- critical: patch plan within 24h, patch applied or mitigated within 72h, auto-escalate at 24h to security manager if not assigned.
- high: patch plan within 72h, applied within 7 days.
- medium: review within 14 days, remediation within 30 days or documented exception.
- low: review within 30 days, track in backlog; auto-close after 180 days with justification summary.

Escalation matrix (simple):
- initial assignment -> product oncall (24/7)
- after SLA miss (first threshold) -> security manager (pager)
- after SLA miss (escalation threshold) -> head of engineering and CISO on email + ticket to exec queue

Patch evidence and retention policy:
- Evidence artifact types: vulnerability scan reports (raw), patch binaries/containers, test logs, verification scripts, ticket/PR links.
- Evidence must be uploaded to encrypted evidence-bucket with KMS key id and content-hash recorded in evidence_hashes.
- Retention: minimum 3 years for audit-relevant evidence; metadata retained indefinitely.
- Access: only vuln_auditor and users explicitly granted access to component evidence may download raw artifacts. Access events recorded in audit stream.

Dependency review automation notes (SCA and third-party libs):
- Normalize SCA output to our internal vulnerability object early (map package name, ecosystem, version, and advisory ids).
- Use dependency fingerprinting to dedupe similar advisories across scanners. Include dependency_lockfile_hash to tie a finding to a specific commit.
- Maintain a component-allowlist where approved transitive dependencies are recorded with approver and expiry. Allowlist entries are surfaced as exceptions in triage.

Rollback tracing and forensics:
- When a patch is rolled back, create a rollback event with rollback_reference and record the patch_version rolled back.
- Correlate deployment traces (CI/CD job ids, deploy manifests) with patch events by tagging patch jobs with deployment_job_id.
- Provide a one-click export for postmortem that includes the vuln events, evidence_refs, and a change timeline.

Operational considerations and implementation plan (next 8 weeks):
- Week 1-2: finalize event schema enums and field list; update scanner adapters to emit required fields.
- Week 3-4: implement RBAC v2 role templates and scoping; add time-limited grant API.
- Week 5: build SIEM parser and index mapping; ingestion performance tests.
- Week 6: rollout triage automation rules for critical/high only; monitor false-positive rate and human overrides.
- Week 7-8: expand automation coverage, implement evidence retention automation and export hooks.

Risks and open questions:
- False auto-remediations on complex packages (need safe-list and manual checkpoints).
- Evidence volume growth — must ensure evidence-bucket lifecycle policies and dedupe by hash to control storage.
- RBAC scoping complexity for cross-functional teams (need a small pilot of 2 product teams first).

Action items:
- Aisha: draft final enum list and circulate to scanner owners by 2027-02-18.
- Matt: prototype SIEM sourcetype and ingestion dashboard by 2027-02-25.
- Claire: run RBAC pilot with infra and platform teams (2 components) and report issues by 2027-03-04.
- Dev: create PR for vulnerability ingest normalization (github.com/redwood-inference/vuln-ingest) and attach to JIRA-SEC-8912.

Appendix: quick grep patterns for SIEM alerts to detect SLA breaches:
- search: index=sec_vuln_lifecycle event_type=sla_violation OR (event_type=triage_update AND sla_deadline<now AND severity_after=critical)
- alert: create ticket to JIRA-SEC with vuln_id and event_id, include evidence_refs and assign to product oncall.

Document history:
- 2027-02-10: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2027-02-12: added RBAC role templates (Matt)
- 2027-02-14: SIEM mapping and action items added (Claire)

Open: please add comments inline and flag any scanner that cannot emit the minimum fields above.
